note: How to get each chat app and make its bot, one recipe per channel Branch supports. Only official packages and links. See docs/configuration.md, Setting up a chat app in one command.

recipes.name: Telegram
recipes.what: Message Branch from Telegram, through a bot of your own.

create.how: BotFather opens with /newbot already typed. Send it, then give the bot a name and a username ending in bot. BotFather answers with the token.

paste.what: The token BotFather sends: digits, a colon, then a long run of letters

recipes.pairing: Send any message to your bot in Telegram. It answers with a six-digit code; type that code here.

recipes.name: Discord
recipes.what: Message Branch in Discord, through a bot you invite to your server.

create.how: Name the application, open Bot, press Reset Token and copy it. Switch on Message Content Intent on the same page. To invite it, pick the bot and applications.commands scopes under OAuth2, URL Generator, so Branch's commands show in Discord's / picker.

paste.what: The bot token from the Bot page

recipes.pairing: Invite the bot to your server and send it a direct message. It answers with a six-digit code; approve it under Customize, Chat apps.

recipes.name: Slack
recipes.what: Message Branch in Slack, through an app in your workspace.

create.how: Slack opens its new-app page with Branch's settings filled in. Pick your workspace and press Create, then Install. Copy the Bot User OAuth Token, and under Basic Information make an app-level token with connections:write.

slash_commands.description: Send Branch a command: /branch status, /branch new, /branch help

paste.what: The Bot User OAuth Token, starting xoxb-

recipes.pairing: Send the app a direct message in Slack. It answers with a six-digit code; approve it under Customize, Chat apps.

recipes.name: WhatsApp Business
recipes.what: Message Branch on WhatsApp, through a WhatsApp Business number.

create.how: Make a Meta app with the WhatsApp product, then copy the access token, the phone number ID and the app secret from its pages.

fields.name: phoneNumberId
fields.what: The phone number ID shown under WhatsApp, API Setup

paste.what: A word of your own choosing, typed into WhatsApp's webhook page too

recipes.noCheck: Meta's read-only check needs the token inside the address, which Branch never does, so the token is checked when WhatsApp first posts to Branch.
recipes.pairing: Send a WhatsApp message to the business number. It answers with a six-digit code; approve it under Customize, Chat apps.

recipes.name: Email
recipes.what: Email Branch, and it answers by email.
recipes.noApp: Any mail program works, and Branch reads the mailbox itself, so there is nothing to install.
recipes.noCreate: Each mail service has its own page for app passwords; Branch cannot pick one for you.
steps: Turn on two-step sign-in with your mail service.
Make an app password on its security page (Google: myaccount.google.com/apppasswords).
Type the address and your mail service's IMAP and SMTP server names here (Gmail: imap.gmail.com and smtp.gmail.com), then paste the app password.

paste.what: The app password (not your usual password)

recipes.noCheck: Mail is checked by signing in to the IMAP server when it connects, not by a web request; a wrong password is said when it connects.

fields.name: address
fields.what: The email address Branch reads and answers from

fields.name: imapHost
fields.what: The IMAP server name, for example imap.gmail.com

fields.name: smtpHost
fields.what: The SMTP server name, for example smtp.gmail.com

recipes.name: Facebook Messenger
recipes.what: Message Branch through your Facebook Page on Messenger.
recipes.noApp: Messenger's desktop app has been retired; the page is managed on the web.

create.how: Make a Meta app with the Messenger product, link your page, and copy the page access token and the app secret.

paste.what: A word of your own choosing, typed into Meta's webhook page too

recipes.noCheck: Meta's read-only check needs the token inside the address, which Branch never does.

recipes.name: Instagram
recipes.what: Message Branch through your professional Instagram account.
recipes.noApp: Instagram has no desktop app to install; messages are handled through Meta's developer site.

create.how: Make a Meta app with Instagram messaging for your professional account, then copy its token and app secret.

paste.what: A word of your own choosing, typed into Meta's webhook page too

recipes.noCheck: Meta's read-only check needs the token inside the address, which Branch never does.

recipes.name: Matrix (Element)
recipes.what: Message Branch in Matrix, through an account of its own on your homeserver.

create.how: Make a separate account for the assistant on your homeserver, sign in with it, and copy its access token from Settings, Help and About.

fields.name: server
fields.what: Your homeserver's address, for example https://matrix.org

recipes.name: Signal
recipes.what: Message Branch on Signal, through signal-cli on this computer.
recipes.noCreate: Signal has no bot API. Branch talks through signal-cli, a separate open-source program (not made by Signal) that you install yourself; Branch never installs it.
steps: Install signal-cli from its own releases page (github.com/AsamK/signal-cli).
Link it to your phone's Signal as a new device, or register a second number with it.
Type the full path to signal-cli and the number here.
recipes.noCheck: Nothing to paste: signal-cli holds the account itself.

recipes.name: Mattermost

create.how: In your Mattermost, open Integrations, add an incoming webhook for a channel and copy its address; add an outgoing webhook too if the assistant should answer.

recipes.noCheck: The only way to test an incoming address is to post a message into your chat, so Branch checks that it is an https address and leaves the first message to you.

fields.name: server
fields.what: The address of your own server, starting with https://

fields.name: server

create.how: Make a Messaging API channel, then copy its channel access token and channel secret.
Create a bot account through Viber's partner site and copy its token.

recipes.name: IRC
steps: Pick a network, for example Libera.Chat.
Register the assistant's nick with the network (Libera.Chat: /msg NickServ REGISTER).
Paste its password here if it has one.

fields.name: server
fields.what: The network's server name, like irc.libera.chat

recipes.noCreate: IRC networks register nicks by chat command, not on a web page.
recipes.noCheck: There is nothing Branch can ask a web service to check; the connection is tried when the switch goes on.
recipes.noApp: IRC is an open protocol with many programs; Branch connects by itself, so nothing needs installing.

recipes.name: Twitch chat
recipes.noApp: Twitch chat runs in the browser; Branch connects by itself.

create.how: Register an application, then make a user access token for the bot's account with the chat:read and chat:edit scopes.

paste.what: The bot account's user access token

recipes.name: Gotify
recipes.noApp: Gotify is a server you run yourself; its phone app is the only thing to install.

create.how: In your Gotify, open Apps, create an application and copy its token.

fields.name: server
fields.what: The address of your own server, starting with https://

recipes.noCheck: An application token can only send, so there is no read-only check; the first message is the test.

recipes.name: iMessage
steps: Only on a Mac: sign in to Messages with your Apple Account.
Let Branch read Messages (System Settings, Privacy and Security, Full Disk Access) and control it (Automation).
recipes.noCreate: Messages has no bot to create: the assistant answers as you, on your own Mac.
recipes.noCheck: There is nothing Branch can ask a web service to check; the connection is tried when the switch goes on.
recipes.noApp: Messages comes with every Mac; there is nothing to install.

recipes.name: iMessage through BlueBubbles
steps: On a Mac that stays on and is signed in to Messages, install the BlueBubbles server app from bluebubbles.app and finish its own setup.

In the BlueBubbles server, copy its https address (its Cloudflare or dynamic DNS link) and the server password. The Mac's address on your own network works only once private addresses are allowed under Computer → Network reach.
Paste them here. Branch asks the server for new messages every few seconds and sends through it with AppleScript, so the Mac does not need BlueBubbles' Private API.
recipes.noCreate: There is no account to create: BlueBubbles runs on your own Mac and answers as your Apple Account. It is a separate open-source app, not made by Apple; Branch never installs it.
recipes.noCheck: The BlueBubbles server takes its password only in the address, so the setup page does not send it anywhere to test; it is tried when the switch goes on, and a wrong password is named on the card.
recipes.noApp: Nothing to install on this computer: the BlueBubbles server runs on the Mac, and you keep using Messages on your phone.

create.how: In the Teams Developer Portal, open Bot management, add a bot, make a client secret, and copy the bot id and the secret.
Sign in to Webex for Developers, create a bot and copy its access token.

paste.what: A secret of your own for the webhook

recipes.name: Synology Chat

fields.name: server
fields.what: The address of your own server, starting with https://

recipes.name: Zalo Official Account

create.how: Make an app on Zalo for Developers, link your Official Account, and copy the app secret, the OA secret key and the tokens.

recipes.noCheck: Zalo's check would spend the refresh token, so Branch leaves it for the first connection.

recipes.name: Flock

create.how: Sign in to Flock's developer site, create an app with a bot, and copy the app secret and the bot token.

recipes.noCheck: Flock does not document a read-only check for a bot token.

recipes.name: Pumble

create.how: Create a Pumble app for your workspace and copy its app key, bot token and signing secret.

recipes.noCheck: Pumble does not document a read-only check for a bot token.

recipes.noApp: Mastodon runs in the browser; the phone app is optional.

create.how: Your server opens its new-application page. Give it a name, keep read and write, save, and copy Your access token.

fields.name: server
fields.what: Your Mastodon server, for example https://mastodon.social

recipes.name: Bluesky
recipes.noApp: Bluesky runs in the browser; the phone app is optional.

recipes.noCheck: Checking an app password means signing in, which Branch does when the switch goes on.

recipes.name: Reddit
recipes.noApp: Reddit runs in the browser; the phone app is optional.

recipes.noCheck: Reddit's check means signing in, which Branch does when the switch goes on.

recipes.name: Discourse
recipes.noApp: Discourse is a forum in the browser; nothing to install.

create.how: Your forum opens its new API key page (admins only). Give it a description, choose the assistant's user, and copy the key.

fields.name: username
fields.what: The forum user the assistant acts as

recipes.name: X direct messages
recipes.noApp: X runs in the browser; the phone app is optional.

create.how: In the X developer portal, make an app with direct-message access and make a user access token for the bot's account. X charges for this API.

recipes.name: Twist

create.how: Make a Twist integration, or a test token from its OAuth section, and copy the access token.

fields.name: conversation
fields.what: The id of the conversation to answer in

recipes.noCheck: Twist's read-only check was not confirmed in its documentation, so Branch does not guess one.

create.how: Your Nextcloud opens on Security. Make an app password for the assistant's account and copy it.

fields.name: room
fields.what: The conversation token from the room's address

recipes.name: Text messages (Twilio)
recipes.noApp: Twilio is a web service; nothing to install.

create.how: In the Twilio Console, copy the Account SID and Auth Token, and buy or pick a number.

recipes.name: ntfy
recipes.noApp: ntfy needs no desktop program; the phone app shows the notifications.
recipes.noCreate: ntfy needs no account: you choose a hard-to-guess topic name and subscribe to it in the phone app.
steps: Choose a long, hard-to-guess topic name.
Subscribe to it in the ntfy phone app.

paste.what: An access token, only for a server that asks for one

recipes.noCheck: A public topic has nothing to check; the first notification is the test.

recipes.name: Pushover
recipes.noApp: Pushover's desktop client runs in the browser; the phone app shows the notifications.

create.how: Pushover opens its new-application page. Name it Branch, create it, and copy its API token. Your user key is on the Pushover home page.

recipes.name: Threema Gateway

create.how: Sign up for Threema Gateway, request a Basic ID, and copy the ID and its secret.

recipes.noCheck: Threema's check needs the secret inside the address, which Branch never does.

create.how: Your Home Assistant opens on Security. Under Long-lived access tokens, create one and copy it.

recipes.name: XMPP (Jabber)
steps: Make an account for the assistant on an XMPP server.
Paste its password here.
recipes.noCreate: XMPP accounts are made on the server you choose; there is no single sign-up page.
recipes.noCheck: There is nothing Branch can ask a web service to check; the connection is tried when the switch goes on.
recipes.noApp: XMPP is an open protocol with many programs (xmpp.org lists them); Branch connects by itself, so nothing needs installing.

recipes.name: MQTT
steps: Use the MQTT broker you already run (for example Mosquitto).
Make a user for the assistant and paste its password here.
recipes.noCreate: A broker is yours to run; there is nothing to create on a web page.
recipes.noCheck: There is nothing Branch can ask a web service to check; the connection is tried when the switch goes on.
recipes.noApp: MQTT is a message protocol, not an app; Branch connects to your broker by itself.

recipes.name: Keybase
steps: Install Keybase and sign in with the assistant's account.
Type the full path to the keybase program here.

fields.name: path
fields.what: The full path to the keybase program

recipes.noCreate: Keybase bots are ordinary accounts made in the Keybase app.
recipes.noCheck: Nothing to paste: the keybase program holds the account.

steps: Install SimpleX Chat on your phone and connect to the assistant's address once it runs.

recipes.noCreate: SimpleX has no accounts to create; the assistant's address is made by simplex-chat.
recipes.noCheck: Nothing to paste: SimpleX has no tokens.

Install deltachat-rpc-server (Delta Chat's own releases) for the assistant and type its full path here; Branch does not install it.
recipes.noCreate: Delta Chat uses an email-like account made inside the program; there is no bot page.
recipes.noCheck: Nothing to paste: the program holds the account.

Paste the key (nsec or hex) here.
recipes.noCreate: Nostr keys are made by programs, not on a sign-up page.
recipes.noCheck: There is nothing Branch can ask a web service to check; the connection is tried when the switch goes on.
recipes.noApp: Nostr is an open protocol with many programs; Branch connects by itself.

recipes.noApp: VK runs in the browser; the phone app is optional.

Sign in to the QQ bot platform, create a bot, and copy its AppID and AppSecret.

recipes.name: Mumble
steps: Install Mumble to talk to the assistant.
Give Branch the server name and a username for the assistant.

paste.what: The server password, if there is one

recipes.noCreate: Mumble has no accounts to create; the assistant joins a server by name.

recipes.name: WeChat Official Account

create.how: In your verified Official Account's developer settings, copy the AppSecret, set a Token and EncodingAESKey, and choose safe mode.

recipes.noCheck: WeChat only takes the AppSecret inside the address, which Branch never does, so it is checked on first connection.

recipes.name: WeCom app

create.how: In the WeCom admin console, make a self-built app, and copy its Secret; under Receive messages set a Token and EncodingAESKey.

recipes.noCheck: WeCom only takes the secret inside the address, which Branch never does, so it is checked on first connection.
